title: Washington Just Ordered Anthropic to Shut Down Its Most Powerful AI Models. Foreign Nationals Need Not Apply.
excerpt: The Commerce Department's export control directive blocks all non-Americans from accessing Fable 5 and Mythos 5 — including H-1B holders working inside the United States.
body:
The U.S. Commerce Department on Friday issued an export control directive ordering Anthropic to immediately suspend access to its two most advanced artificial intelligence models — Fable 5 and Mythos 5 — for all foreign nationals, citing national security concerns.

Anthropic complied within hours, but did so by disabling the models for everyone, not just non-Americans. The company said separating users by citizenship on short notice was not technically feasible.

"The net effect of this order is that we must abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all our customers to ensure compliance," Anthropic said in a statement. "Access to all other Anthropic models will not be affected."

The shutdown marks the most aggressive step the U.S. government has taken to restrict access to frontier AI software itself — as opposed to the chips and hardware that power it. For years, American export controls have targeted semiconductors and manufacturing equipment. This order targets the models directly.

## A Jailbreak the Company Calls Overblown

The government's stated concern centres on a method of bypassing safety guardrails — known as a "jailbreak" — that could allow Fable 5 to identify software vulnerabilities. Anthropic pushed back hard on the severity of the finding.

The company said it had reviewed the technique and found it surfaced "a small number of previously known, minor vulnerabilities" that other publicly available models, including OpenAI's GPT-5.5, can also find without any bypass. Anthropic received only "verbal evidence" of the issue and was not given written documentation of the specific national security concern.



> **""We disagree that the finding of a narrow potential jailbreak should be cause for recalling a commercial model deployed to hundreds of millions of people," the company said."**


"We disagree that the finding of a narrow potential jailbreak should be cause for recalling a commercial model deployed to hundreds of millions of people," the company said.

## The Citizenship Test for AI

The directive applies to "any foreign national, wherever located, inside or outside the United States, including foreign national Anthropic employees," the company confirmed. Dean Ball, a former White House official who helped draft the administration's 2025 AI Action Plan, noted the implication on X: "This means you should expect to have to prove your citizenship to use Anthropic models."

That formulation lands squarely on the hundreds of thousands of skilled workers in the United States on H-1B and other work visas — a population disproportionately Indian. Indians account for over 70 per cent of all approved H-1B petitions annually. Many work at companies that have integrated Anthropic's Claude models into their workflows, and some work at Anthropic itself.

Several prominent Anthropic leaders were born outside the United States. The company declined to comment on whether they could access the models under the directive.

Amazon's cloud unit AWS confirmed late Friday that Anthropic had asked it to revoke access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for "all users in all regions."

## A Broader Pattern of AI Nationalism

The order arrives against a backdrop of escalating tensions between AI developers and the Trump administration. Anthropic's relationship with the government fractured earlier this year after the company refused to allow the U.S. military to use its AI models for domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons systems. Washington responded by placing Anthropic on a Pentagon supply chain blacklist, set to take effect later in the year.

Just ten days before the export control order, President Trump signed an executive order establishing a framework for the federal government to vet the national security risks of frontier AI systems for up to a month before their public release. Participation was described as voluntary — but the Anthropic action suggests the government is prepared to use compulsory tools.

"If this standard was applied across the industry, we believe it would essentially halt all new model deployments for all frontier model providers," Anthropic warned.

## What This Means for India's Tech Workforce

The directive does not name any specific country. But its effect is felt most acutely in India's technology ecosystem — both in the United States and at home.

Indian engineers and researchers constitute the largest single-nationality cohort of AI professionals in Silicon Valley. TCS announced just this week that it would give 50,000 employees access to Anthropic's Claude models as part of a workforce transformation programme. Indian startups building on Claude's API — including several in the government's IndiaAI mission — now face uncertainty about whether their access to Anthropic's frontier tools will be restored, and on what terms.

Anthropic called the situation a "misunderstanding" and said it is working to restore access as soon as possible. But the precedent is set: the U.S. government can, with a single directive, shut down a commercial AI model for the entire world and sort users by passport.
